item.subject: Advanced Mathematics
item.stem:
Two mathematical models are proposed to predict the return y, in dollars, from the sale of x thousand units of an article (where 0 < x < 5). Each of these models, P and Q, is based on different marketing methods.

model P:   y = 6x − x^2
model Q:   y = 2x

For what values of x does model Q predict a greater return than model P?

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
A radio-active element decomposes according to the formula,

y = y_o e^(-kt)

where y is the mass of the element remaining after t days and y_o is the value of y for t = 0.

Find the value of the constant k for an element whose half-life (i.e. time to decompose half of the material) is 4 days.

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
[Image: Graph of f(x) on a coordinate plane with shaded regions A, B, and C]

For the areas between the graph of f(x) and the x-axis shown above, area A = 4.8 units, area B = 0.8 units, and area C = 2 units.

What is the value of the definite integral integral from -2 to 4 of f(x) dx?
reference_items.figure_description:
A coordinate grid with horizontal x-axis and vertical f(x)-axis intersecting at origin O. Both axes have grid lines every 1 unit, with markings every 2 units: on the x-axis from -4 to 4, and on the f(x)-axis from -4 to 4. A curve representing the function f is plotted on the grid:
- It passes through (-4, -2), rises to cross the x-axis at (-2, 0), reaches a local maximum at (0, 2), and goes down to cross the x-axis at (2, 0).
- It dips below the x-axis to a local minimum near (2.5, -1), then crosses the x-axis back up at (3, 0).
- It rises sharply to a peak at (3.5, 3), and comes down to cross the x-axis at (4, 0), continuing downward below the x-axis.
Three regions bounded by the curve and the x-axis are shaded:
- Region A is vertically shaded, lying above the x-axis between x = -2 and x = 2.
- Region B is diagonally shaded, lying below the x-axis between x = 2 and x = 3.
- Region C is horizontally shaded, lying above the x-axis between x = 3 and x = 4.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data.

reference_items.subject: Advanced Mathematics
reference_items.stem:
Which of the following graphs has these features:
f'(0) > 0, f'(1) < 0, and f''(x) is always negative?

options.label: A
options.text: [Image: Downward-opening curve entirely below the x-axis]

options.label: B
options.text: [Image: Upward-opening curve entirely above the x-axis]

options.label: C
options.text: [Image: Curve with a maximum on the y-axis and a minimum for x > 1]

options.label: E
options.text: [Image: Curve with a local minimum for x < 0 and a local maximum between 0 and 1]

reference_items.figure_description:
Five Cartesian coordinate systems labeled A through E, each with a horizontal x-axis and a vertical y-axis, and a tick mark labeled 1 on the positive x-axis:
- Graph A shows a curve concave downward everywhere, located entirely below the x-axis, with its vertex (maximum) between x = 0 and x = 1. At x = 0 the slope is positive, and at x = 1 the slope is negative.
- Graph B shows a curve concave upward everywhere, located entirely above the x-axis, with its vertex (minimum) between x = 0 and x = 1.
- Graph C shows a curve with a local maximum on the y-axis at x = 0, which decreases, crosses the x-axis, reaches a local minimum to the right of x = 1, and then curves upward.
- Graph D shows a curve that decreases strictly from left to right, concave downward everywhere, crossing the y-axis with a negative slope and crossing the x-axis to the left of x = 1.
- Graph E shows a curve that has a local minimum for x < 0, increases through the y-axis with a positive slope at x = 0, reaches a local maximum between x = 0 and x = 1, and decreases through x = 1.
reference_items.calibration: Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data.

slope.instructions: TIMSS scaled this 1-point item with the three-parameter logistic (3PL) model, which TIMSS uses for multiple-choice items, in the calibration "Concurrent scaling of the TIMSS Advanced 1995 and 2008 advanced mathematics data". What is the item's slope (discrimination) parameter a? A higher a means that the item separates students of lower and higher mathematics ability more sharply. Choose the value closest to it. The state also lists reference items: the calibrated TIMSS items of the same grade most similar to this one (never the item itself or its other parts), most similar first, with their percent correct and their calibrated parameters, each on the scale of its own calibration. Use them to place this item.
